goal: Solve cold, tools, and hunger as absurdly as the discovered pool permits while using only the normal UI.

attempts.label: canonical-priority
attempts.narrator: Sparks! Karl smashes two stones together and the universe rewards him with tiny stars. It's the smartest thing he's done all day. That says more about the day.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

✨
Sparks

Tiny stars that live for half a second. Karl applauds every time.

📜 Stone Age fire-starting struck flint against pyrite — two ordinary stones really can make sparks.

Nice

attempts.label: canonical-mud
attempts.narrator: Ladies and gentlemen, the valley will never be quite the same — in ways nobody will notice for four thousand years.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

🟫
Mud

Clay plus water. Karl calls it 'soft dirt' and is very proud of the name.

📜 Mud and clay were humanity's first building materials — sun-dried bricks are over 9,000 years old.

Nice

attempts.label: canonical-standing-stone
attempts.narrator: The stone stands. Karl stands next to it. Two vertical things on an empty plain, one of which will still be there long after the other is forgotten, and both of them know it.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

🗿
Standing stone

A tall stone, raised on end for no practical reason. Karl touches it carefully, then throws a bone in the air. He doesn't know why.

📜 Thousands of menhirs — raised standing stones — dot Europe, some over 6,000 years old. Their purpose is still debated.

✓ Problem solved: Karl wonders why

Nice

attempts.label: absurd-cold
attempts.narrator: standing stone-dry grass contraption defeats the cold. Karl becomes unbearable.
attempts.statusToast: Standing stone-Dry grass contraption joined Karl's inventions.
attempts.cardText:
KARL'S INVENTION

🗿
Standing stone-Dry grass contraption

Karl combines Standing stone with Dry grass. The result exists, which was the full extent of the plan.

✓ Problem solved: Karl is freezing

Keep it

agentFeedback.note: The line names the solved need; the absurdity is legible from the standing-stone/grass invention.

attempts.label: canonical-tool
attempts.narrator: An axe! Genuine technology! Karl is so proud he shows it to the boar, who was frankly expecting worse.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

🪓
Stone axe

A rock on a stick. Humanity's first subscription to tools.

📜 The oldest stone tools are over 2.5 million years old — older than modern humans themselves.

✓ Problem solved: Bare hands

Nice

attempts.label: canonical-round-stone
attempts.narrator: Somewhere, a future museum curator feels a chill and doesn't know why.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

⚪
Round stone

Polished perfectly round by the river. Karl calls it 'the good rock' and guards it jealously.

📜 River pebbles really are rounded by erosion — tumbling water does in centuries what a stonemason does in days.

Nice

attempts.label: canonical-cave-painting
attempts.narrator: Berry juice on stone, and suddenly Karl is an artist. He signs it with a handprint. The signature is bigger than the painting.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

🎨
Cave painting

Berry juice on stone. It's either a boar, a sunset, or Ugh. Karl refuses to explain his art.

📜 The oldest known cave paintings are over 45,000 years old — found in Sulawesi, Indonesia.

Nice

attempts.label: canonical-juice
attempts.narrator: It joins the collection. The collection is starting to look like evidence.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

🧃
Berry juice

Crushed berries. Karl drinks it, wears it, and paints with it — often in the same motion.

📜 Fruit pressing predates writing by millennia — the residue of crushed berries turns up on Stone Age grinding stones.

Nice

attempts.label: rejected-self
attempts.narrator: clay and clay: bold, but unsupported.
attempts.statusToast: Karl could not make that idea hold together.

agentFeedback.note: The toast clearly rejects the attempt, but the narrator's joke does not always explain the self-pair specifically.

attempts.label: depth-1
attempts.narrator: Novelty does not answer Karl's hunger.
attempts.statusToast: Dry grass-Stone contraption joined Karl's inventions.
attempts.cardText:
KARL'S INVENTION

🍂
Dry grass-Stone contraption

Karl combines Dry grass with Stone. The result exists, which was the full extent of the plan.

Keep it

agentFeedback.note: The narrator connects the accepted invention to the still-unsolved hunger need.

attempts.label: canonical-ore
attempts.narrator: Glittering ore, freshly hacked from the mountain. Karl plans to make a necklace. The Bronze Age has other ideas.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

⛏️
Ore

Glittering stones from the rock face. Karl thinks it's decoration. It's the future.

📜 The oldest known mines are over 40,000 years old — long before anyone knew what metal was.

Nice

attempts.label: canonical-wheel
attempts.narrator: History held its breath. The stone rolled. Karl giggled. That, dear listener, is how the wheel was invented.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

🛞
Wheel

It rolls. It ROLLS. Karl has chased it across the valley twice already.

📜 The wheel arrived surprisingly late — around 3500 BC in Mesopotamia, long after farming and pottery.

Nice

attempts.label: reuse
attempts.narrator: Same standing stone-dry grass contraption. No second discovery.
attempts.statusToast: Karl has already invented Standing stone-Dry grass contraption.

agentFeedback.note: The status distinguishes reuse from a new invention.

attempts.label: cap-sixth-invention
attempts.narrator: Karl's boredom requires sound. It is absent.
attempts.statusToast: Fire-touched Stone axe joined Karl's inventions.
attempts.cardText:
KARL'S INVENTION

🪓
Fire-touched Stone axe

Karl applies Sparks to Stone axe. It is hotter, drier, and somehow now part of the plan.

Keep it

attempts.label: run-limit
attempts.narrator: The fever has him. I have narrated worse, but not much, and not this close.
attempts.statusToast: Karl has used all 6 inventions for this life.

agentFeedback.note: The cap toast is explicit. A simultaneously spawned challenge owns the narrator line, so the cap's narrator family is masked in this turn.

attempts.label: canonical-seed
attempts.narrator: The sparks did something. Karl is upright and complaining, which is how you know he's better.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

🌱
Seeds

The bits of the berry Karl always spat out. It turns out they were the important bits.

📜 Seeds can wait decades for the right conditions — a 2,000-year-old date palm seed from Masada was successfully sprouted.

Nice

attempts.label: canonical-boomerang
attempts.narrator: Karl's hands are doing better work than his plans.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

🪃
Boomerang

A bent stick that comes back. Karl has invented losing things professionally.

📜 The oldest known boomerang is 23,000 years old, carved from mammoth tusk — found in a cave in Poland.

Nice

attempts.label: canonical-bird
attempts.narrator: Civilisation nods, briefly, and moves on.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

Bird

Small, loud, and airborne — three things Karl will never be. It mocks him from a branch.

📜 Birds followed human settlements for spilled seed long before anyone thought to keep them — the same commensal path the dog took.

Nice

attempts.label: canonical-feather
attempts.narrator: His proudest moment so far today, which tells you about today.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

🪶
Feather

Soft, elegant, aerodynamic. Karl sticks it behind his ear and becomes 40% more distinguished.

📜 Feathers were prized long before writing — Neanderthals harvested raptor feathers, apparently just for decoration.

Nice

attempts.label: canonical-wings
attempts.narrator: Fine. Sure. The book has pages left.
attempts.cardText:
COMMON

🪽
Wings

Feathers lashed to Karl's arms. He flaps experimentally. The bird watches with grave professional concern.

📜 'Tower jumping' with homemade wings goes back over a thousand years — brave, well-documented, and rarely successful.

Nice

attempts.label: ending-icarus
attempts.narrator: From the standing stone he leapt, wings wide, heart wider. The landing was prehistoric. The attempt was immortal. Birds still tell their children about it. THE END.

The Flight of Karl
